clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old man with longstanding secondary hyperparathyroidism and renal failure on hemodialysis developed refractory hypercalcemia (albumin corrected calcium 3.96 mmol/l) and elevated alkaline phosphatase (160 u/l), indicating hypercalcemic crisis and tertiary hyperparathyroidism. Postoperative follow-up showed stable normalization of calcium and PTH levels. Histopathology after parathyroidectomy revealed a 2 cm well-encapsulated parathyroid mass composed mainly of chief cells consistent with a parathyroid adenoma. Clinical symptoms including restless legs syndrome and GI distress resolved after surgery. Pre-surgery intact PTH and biochemical calcium-PTH set-point data were not documented.
